sentences.text: 2. Petitioners are the accused in Crime No.103/2025 of Thiruvalla Police Station.

The above case is registered against the petitioners alleging offences punishable under Sections 465, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code (for short, IPC) and later the offences under Sections 120(b), 511 and 420 of IPC were added.
3. The prosecution case is that the accused created forged treatment records for getting money from the Chief Ministers' Relief Fund in the name of Devika D/o Sreekumar.

4. Heard counsel for the petitioners and the Public Prosecutor.
2025:KER:10131 BAIL APPL. NO. 1212 OF 2025 5.
The counsel for the petitioners submitted that the allegation against the petitioners are not correct.
The husband of the 2nd accused, who is a carpenter, is a heart patient and had undergone surgery.

During the course of treatment at various hospitals, one person who introduced himself as an employee of the Medical College told the 2 nd accused who was accompanying her sister in the hospital that there is provision for getting money from Chief Minister's Relief Fund and collected certain documents.
Actually the petitioners were cheated by that person.
The counsel submitted that the petitioners are ready to abide any conditions if this Court grant them bail.
The Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application.
6. This Court considered the contentions of the petitioners and the Public Prosecutor.
It is true that the allegation in the complaint is serious.
But whether the petitioners are involved in this case is a matter to be investigated.
I do not want to make any observation about the same.
The prosecution can prove the case through oral and documentary evidence.
Custodial interrogation of the petitioners is not necessary.
The petitioners are ladies.

Moreover, it is a well accepted principle that the bail is the rule and the jail is the exception.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Chidambaram.

P v Directorate of Enforcement [2019 (16) SCALE 870],
after considering all the earlier judgments, observed that, the basic jurisprudence relating to bail remains the same inasmuch as the grant of bail is the rule and refusal is the exception so as to ensure that the accused has the opportunity of securing fair trial.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

8. Recently the Apex Court in Siddharth v State of Uttar Pradesh and Another [2021(5)KHC 353]
considered the point in detail.

entities.text: Siddharth v State of Uttar Pradesh and Another [2021(5)KHC 353]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relevant paragraph of the above judgment is extracted hereunder:
"12. We may note that personal liberty is an important aspect of our constitutional mandate.

The occasion to arrest an accused during investigation arises when custodial investigation becomes necessary or it is a heinous crime or where there is a possibility of influencing the witnesses or accused may abscond.
Merely because an arrest can be made because it is lawful does not mandate that arrest must be made.
A distinction must be made 2025:KER:10131 BAIL APPL. NO. 1212 OF 2025 between the existence of the power to arrest and the justification for exercise of it.

(Joginder Kumar v. State of UP and Others (1994 KHC 189: (1994) 4 SCC 260:
1994 (1) KLT 919: 1994 (2) KLJ 97: AIR 1994 SC 1349: 1994 CriLJ 1981))

entities.text:
Joginder Kumar v. State of UP and Others (1994 KHC 189: (1994) 4 SCC 260:
1994 (1) KLT 919: 1994 (2) KLJ 97: AIR 1994 SC 1349: 1994 CriLJ 1981
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If arrest is made routine, it can cause incalculable harm to the reputation and self-esteem of a person.

If the Investigating Officer has no reason to believe that the accused will abscond or disobey summons and has, in fact, throughout cooperated with the investigation we fail to appreciate why there should be a compulsion on the officer to arrest the accused."
9.

In Manish Sisodia v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2023 KHC 6961], the Apex Court observed that even if the allegation is one of grave economic offence, it is not a rule that bail should be denied in every case.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2023 KHC 6961]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
10. Considering the dictum laid down in the above decision and considering the facts and circumstances of this case, this Bail Application is allowed with the following directions:
2025:KER:10131 BAIL APPL. NO. 1212 OF 2025 1.
The petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer within two weeks from today and shall undergo interrogation.

2. After interrogation, if the Investigating Officer propose to arrest the petitioners,
they shall be released on bail on executing a bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) each with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the arresting officer concerned.
